item.title: [212] /pkp/ - Pokopia General #10
item.description:
>Hoppip, Skiploom, and Jumpluff Event Live Now (March 9 - March 24, 2026)
https://www.pokemon.com/us/pokemon-news/play-a-limited-time-event-in-pokemon-pokopia-on-nintendo-switch-2

>F.A.Q

>Can I have more than one world in the same console?
Yes. You can have different saves for each profile. It's not like AC.

>What about cloud saves?
Yes. Unlike every other Pokémon game, this one does support cloud saves.

>Does it feature a real time clock? Can I change the console's date to progress faster?
Yes. There's no downside to moving forward or backward.

>Is my favorite Pokemon in?
List is still being updated https://www.serebii.net/pokemonpokopia/availablepokemon.shtml

>I didn't like ACNH, will I like this one?
Similarities with ACNH end at the UI; game is a lot faster, with more activities and a proper ~40h long story mode. If you've played DQ Builders 2, you know what you're getting into.

>Combat? Breakable tools?
No combat, no breakable tools. There's a stamina system in place, but it's very easy to manage.

The oil market sent a clear signal this week that a massive release of stockpiled crude by the U.S. and its allies is nowhere near enough to address the unprecedented supply disruption triggered by the Iran war.

More than 30 nations in Europe, North America and Northeast Asia agreed to flood the market with 400 million barrels of oil in an effort to keep a lid on rising energy prices. The U.S. is leading the effort with a release of 172 million barrels from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve or 43% of the IEA total.

It is the largest release of stockpiled oil in the 50-year history of the International Energy Agency, an organization tasked with maintaining the energy security of its members during global crises.

But the oil bazooka is not inspiring confidence in the market. Crude prices have surged more than 17% since the IEA announced the emergency stockpile release on Wednesday. Brent oil prices, the international benchmark, closed above $100 on Friday for the second session in a row.

You feel entitled to go out and be in nature and treat it like your personal fucking playground, damaging the ecosystem and demanding roads and trails be paved through the wilderness so you can “heckin enjoy it”? And then go home and continue to fuel the 6th mass extinction with your destructive consumerist habits?
Anyway, I planted some Texas native wildflowers today to help the declining pollinator population in my area. What did you do?
